html:
Queen of Castile from 1474 until her death in 1504, who with her husband Ferdinand of Aragon laid the base of a united Spain. The pope later named them the Catholic Monarchs.

She married Ferdinand in secret in 1469, against the wishes of her half-brother King Henry IV, and won Castile in a civil war against Henry's daughter Juana. With Ferdinand king of Aragon, the two crowns were joined in one couple, though each kingdom kept its own laws.

Their reign brought:

  • 1478: the Spanish Inquisition, set up to root out converts from Judaism suspected of keeping their old faith;
  • 1492: the conquest of Granada, the last Muslim state in Spain, ending al-Andalus;
  • 1492: the expulsion of Spain's Jews;
  • 1492: the first voyage of Christopher Columbus, which Isabella backed, and with it Spain's empire in the Americas.

Their daughter Catherine of Aragon married Henry VIII of England, and their grandson Charles V inherited a world empire.
